subject: Follow-up: Model fit + benchmarks (Redwood-verified profiles)
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@acme-retail.com>, Jessica Lee <jessica.lee@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Model fit + benchmarks (Redwood-verified profiles)

Hi Samir / Jessica,

Thanks for your time this morning — good conversation. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery:

- Primary goal: real-time product-assistant for checkout and returns flows (latency sensitive, p99 target ~100ms for 256-token responses).
- Target throughput: sustained ~200 TPS during peak windows (burst to 500 TPS).
- Data constraints: customer PII must remain in-region and audit logs required for SOC 2.

Recommended starting models (based on the prompts you shared):
- rwd-3.7b-q4f16 (balanced quality/latency) — good for structured responses and short summaries.
- rwd-13b-int8 (higher quality, slightly higher latency; consider for escalations).
- rwd-2.9b-latency-optimized (if strict p99 < 80ms is required at cost of some quality).

I've attached our Redwood-verified performance profiles (redwood_model_profiles_v1.pdf) which include TPS baselines and latency percentiles (p50/p90/p95/p99) measured on our dedicated clusters. You can also find the profiles here: https://drive.google.com/sample-redwood-profiles

Next steps I recommend:
1) Marissa (cc'd) will run a short, tailored benchmark using your sample prompt set and a 1-hour synthetic load targeting 200 TPS and share the raw results + recommended config (quantization, batching, cache settings).
2) We'll share the prompt_set_sample.csv used for the bench and a short eval checklist for quality regression monitoring.
3) If the bench looks good, we can schedule a 30-min ops sync to discuss deployment (Dedicated vs Hosted) and cost tradeoffs.

Deliverables timeline: Marissa will aim to share initial results within 48 hours.

Couple quick clarifications for your team to confirm: do you expect many multi-turn contexts >512 tokens? And is on-prem/private deployment a hard requirement or just preferred?

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
alex@redwood.com

Thanks Alex — really helpful recap. A couple of quick questions before Marissa runs the bench:

1) For the rwd-3.7b-q4f16 profile, can you confirm p99 latency at 256 tokens on your dedicated cluster (with KV cache warm)? We need to validate it meets our p99 ~100ms target.
2) How do you typically configure batching for low-latency (e.g., max batch size, adaptive vs fixed)?
3) Are there any known quality regressions when switching from 13b to the 3.7b family for intent classification? We have a portion of traffic that uses fine-grained intent classification for fraud signals.

Also, we have a security questionnaire that the security team will send over; important to make sure the answers line up with SOC 2 evidence.

Appreciate it — Samir
Samir Patel

samir@acme-retail.com
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@acme-retail.com>

Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Model fit + benchmarks (Redwood-verified profiles)

Hi Samir — quick answers inline and next steps below.

1) p99 for rwd-3.7b-q4f16 (256 tokens) on our Dedicated baseline (A100-style nodes, KV cache warm) is ~95-110ms depending on sequence overlap and batching. In our published profile the p99 is 105ms for the 256-token test; you'll see the percentile table in the attached PDF. The tailored benchmark Marissa will run will use your prompt set which may shift those numbers slightly (often lower if prompts have common prefixes).

2) Batching: we use adaptive batching by default with per-model recommended max batch sizes in the profiles. For latency-sensitive workloads we recommend setting max_batch_size to 8–16 and enabling adaptive latency SLOs so the runtime prioritizes low-latency over throughput when needed. We'll include the exact recommended config in the bench report.

3) Quality regressions: moving from 13b to 3.7b can show minor drop in nuanced classification for rare intents. For intent classification we recommend running the eval set (we'll use your labeled examples) and powering critical paths with the 13b variant while using 3.7b for general conversational flows — Redwood routing can split traffic by route to achieve that hybrid. We'll include a short precision/recall table in Marissa's report.

Marissa — can you please schedule the bench and attach the prompt set you used? Samir / Jessica, if you can share the labeled intent eval set (even a subset) that will speed the quality checks.

Best,
Alex

Hi Samir / Jessica — looping back with initial bench plan and ETA.

Plan:
- Run 1-hour synthetic load using your prompt_set_sample.csv at 200 TPS steady-state (burst windows simulated).
- Models: rwd-3.7b-q4f16, rwd-13b-int8, rwd-2.9b-latency-optimized.
- Metrics collected: throughput, p50/p90/p95/p99 latency, CPU/GPU utilization, memory/KV cache hit rate, and per-prompt quality score (on your labeled subset).

ETA: Initial results expected within 24–36 hours. I will attach the raw result archive and a short summary (benchmark_results_initial.zip) and call out any quality regressions observed vs the labeled eval set.

Preliminary note: based on quick smoke tests using a small subset, rwd-3.7b-q4f16 is meeting p50/p90 comfortably; p99 sits near ~110ms with our current batching config. We'll try reducing max_batch_size and enabling eager dispatch for the second run if you need tighter p99.

Next step: Samir / Jessica — please send the labeled intent eval subset when convenient (can be a CSV). Also confirm whether logs must be kept in-region for the bench artifacts so we configure S3 location accordingly.

Thanks — Marissa
